subject.title: Heartbeat skipped reason 'target-none' is misleading when delivery is disabled by default

question: Should OpenClaw keep `reason: "target-none"` and add an additive disabled-delivery hint, or rename the exposed reason itself?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the fix shape changes user-visible diagnostic contract: a rename is simpler and clearer, while an additive hint avoids breaking scripts or users that already parse `target-none`.

options.title: Add a disabled-delivery hint
options.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add an optional human-facing hint or display field, and render it in heartbeat-last/status surfaces with tests.

options.title: Rename the reason
options.body: Change the exposed reason to a clearer value such as `delivery-disabled`, accepting compatibility risk for consumers of the old string.

options.title: Leave output as-is
options.body: Rely on docs to explain `target: "none"`, accepting continued low-priority operator confusion.

recommendation.title: Add a disabled-delivery hint
recommendation.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add an optional human-facing hint or display field, and render it in heartbeat-last/status surfaces with tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the default-target-none behavior and earlier heartbeat/outbound unification, so they are the best available owner for the diagnostic contract choice.
